findings.headline: 11 of 49 charts (random plus targeted 99215) support a lower level than billed; 80% of 99215s are on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions
findings.interpretation: Bills 99215 on 14.5% of 2,390 claims vs 3.6% expected (eb_ratio about 4x). The excess shows up at every complexity level. In the random sample, 4 of 6 charted 99215s were documented at moderate MDM. With the targeted 99215 charts added, the chart rule triggered: 11/49 below billed. Overpayment estimate not quotable: the random sample has only 6 charts in the 99215 stratum, and 8 are needed. No data-quality flags. Coder re-scoring recommended.

findings.headline: Charts match the billed level, but the notes look inflated: 47% address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, and the audit trail shows bulk-created and paste-heavy notes
findings.interpretation: 99215 share 22% vs 5% expected, with 15-24% 99215 even on patients with 0-1 conditions. On paper the charts support the billed level (0/30 below), but note checks show a problem mismatch (47%), late signing (17%), duplicate text (17%), and in the audit trail, 13% bulk-created and 13% paste-heavy notes on the same example claims. Consistent with notes inflated to match the bill. These are rates, not proof; a weaker case than 213, and it needs human coder review.

findings.headline: Highest risk-adjusted outlier (37% 99215), but 29 of 30 random charts support the billed level
findings.interpretation: Excess 99215s at every complexity level. Notes show no inflation signals (problem mismatch 20%). The claims pattern is strong, but the charts don't back an upcoding finding. Could be documentation thoroughness or notes written to the level; worth a human look.

findings.headline: 38% 99215 vs 7% expected, but 29 of 30 random charts support billing
findings.interpretation: Charts and note signals don't support a finding despite the claims outlier.

findings.headline: 24% 99215 vs 6% expected; 2 of 30 charts below billed, which is not a pattern
findings.interpretation: Documentation supports billing; no inflation signals.

findings.headline: 25% 99215 vs 7% expected; 1 of 30 charts below billed, but elevated duplicate text (33%), late signing (20%) and data reviewed without tests on the claim (20%)
findings.interpretation: Charts arrived on the second round after the office first sent a billing ledger. Note signals are elevated but didn't meet the inflation rule. An audit trail could be a next step.

findings.headline: Small practice (121 claims), 36% 99215; 3 of 30 charts below billed
findings.interpretation: Full random sample received after two follow-ups. Documentation mostly supports billing.

findings.headline: 20% 99215 vs 5% expected; 4 of 30 charts below billed, too few 99215s to decide
